basis: Per 100 g, or per 100 ml where the item is a liquid (the `per` field says which). THE CORPUS CONVENTION IS RAW AND DRY: every weight in recipes.json is the raw or dry weight of the ingredient unless its own name says otherwise (tinned, cooked, smoked, pre-packed, jarred, ready-cooked). Items whose names break that convention are listed under `ambiguousState` below.
method: Macros are conserved through cooking; water is not. A plate is therefore costed as plateGrams x (batch macros / batch finished weight), where batch finished weight is sum(listed grams x cookedYield). `cookedYield` exists only to derive finished plate weight and must never be applied to the macros as well - that would double-count.
fibreBasis: AOAC total dietary fibre, which is what UK back-of-pack labelling uses.
saltBasis: Grams of salt (sodium x 2.5), matching the corpus and UK labelling.

confidenceKey.high: A named CoFID / McCance & Widdowson or USDA SR entry, or manufacturer back-of-pack for a branded item.
confidenceKey.medium: A composite, a brand average across UK retailers, or a reference entry adjusted for the state the recipe uses.
confidenceKey.low: Estimated. None of the 194 entries needed this, but two carry wide brand ranges and are called out in `wideRanges`.

ambiguousState: Cooked chicken breast, pre-packed - the only ingredient in the corpus that is weighed COOKED. Costed as a brine-injected pre-packed pack (1.00 g salt/100 g), which is what the ingredient line says.
Smoked mackerel fillets - hot-smoked, ready to eat, not raw.
Ready-cooked king prawns - cooked in brine.
All tinned fish, pulses and vegetables - DRAINED weight, as each recipe specifies.
Wholemeal breadcrumbs - the methods describe blitzing stale bread, so costed as bread (270 kcal/100 g), not dried packet crumb (~350). Worth 25-30 kcal a plate if anyone ever uses a packet.
Potatoes - no variety and no state given. Costed raw, old potatoes.
Eggs - shelled weight, raw, as the corpus states.
ambiguousIdentity: Cod, pollock or coley loin - costed as COD (named first; the dish is a cod braise). Pollock and coley differ by under 2 kcal and 1 g protein per 100 g.
Fresh haddock, pollock or coley - costed as HADDOCK (named first, and the dish is a haddock kedgeree).
Choy sum, pak choi or tenderstem - costed as PAK CHOI (the middle of the three). Tenderstem would add ~35 kcal and 5 g protein across a 600 g batch.
Spinach or kale - costed as SPINACH (named first). Kale wilts far less, so choosing it raises plate weight without raising energy.
Rocket or watercress - costed as ROCKET. Under 1 kcal difference on the plate.
Raw king prawns / Raw peeled king prawns - two spellings of one item. Costed identically; they should be merged.
Apple / Apples - two spellings of one item.
wideRanges: High-protein wraps (plan.html) - 45 g light wraps are 118 kcal / 8 g protein, 60 g wraps 160 kcal / 12 g. Costed at 60 g, which is what the .mix names. This is the largest single uncertainty in the breakfast block.
Red curry paste - 5-11 g salt/100 g across brands; 8.0 used, which is the corpus's own reading.
Ready-made meatballs - 1.0-1.3 g salt/100 g; 1.15 used. Rolling your own from 5% mince takes the plate from ~2.7 g of salt to ~1.3 g.
Potatoes, floury, roasted (plan.html) - lightly oiled roasties finish at ~140 kcal/100 g, generously oiled or goose-fat ones at 200-230. The roast plate should say which.
discardedItems: Limes and Lemons are listed as whole fruit but only the juice and zest are eaten; they are costed at the juice/zest yield, not at whole-fruit composition.
